A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AsymRnR with the same authors and core method. Their text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. v1 ends with references and has no appendix; v2 includes readable Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original CogVideoX generation experiments, VBench scores, computational costs, qualitative comparisons and design ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations on Mochi-1, HunyuanVideo and FastVideo-Hunyuan, including additional metrics and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Both versions use asymmetric Q/KV reduction, bipartite matching, Euclidean similarity, token discarding, precomputed reduction scheduling and matching caching. The new theoretical account, scheduling equations and implementation disclosures do not establish a changed underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate text-to-video generation using the standard VBench prompt suite. Additional generators, output specifications and sampling configurations expand model and protocol coverage without introducing a different dataset or task.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds direct comparisons between unaccelerated Mochi-1, HunyuanVideo and distilled FastVideo-Hunyuan and their AsymRnR variants. ToMe and ToMe-fast remain the competing token-reduction methods on CogVideoX-2B; no ToMe results are added for the RoPE-based models.

E3.justification: v2 adds LPIPS evaluation and experiments with different generators, video specifications, Euler sampling budgets and H100 timing. Appendix B reports 50-step DPM for CogVideoX-5B, whereas v1 specifies DDIM for both CogVideoX variants; this establishes a reported setting revision, not a verified rerun. Cache-table labels shift uniformly from 0–5 to 1–6 while their numerical outcomes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The quantitative design ablations are retained, including the destination-stride and SymRnR-combination tests moved to Appendix C. Qualitative case evidence is replaced and expanded: v2 Figures 6 and 10–13 show additional generation comparisons, including sandwich and bear examples illustrating ToMe blurring and pixelation.

E5.justification: v2 omits v1 Section 5's explicit qualification that output discrepancies persist with the random seed controlled. Confidence-interval shading in the feature-similarity plot remains. Neither version supplies benchmark repeated-run counts, significance tests or performance uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The reported CogVideoX scores and quantitative ablation values are retained. v2 adds LPIPS results, individual VBench dimensions in Table 9, and results for three additional generators. For example, Table 2 reports HunyuanVideo with AsymRnR-fast at 703.29 seconds and 0.8237 VBench versus its unaccelerated reference at 912.98 seconds and 0.8157. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: v2 introduces a KL-divergence account of token reduction, Corollary 3.1's nearest-neighbor estimator and covariance-stationarity assumption, and Appendix A's density-estimation derivation and consistency argument. v1 contains the attention, reduction and caching formulations but no corresponding distributional theory.

C1.justification: The training-free acceleration contribution remains, but v2 newly claims theoretical foundations, occasional generation-quality improvements and demonstrated applicability to step-distilled models. These extend the contribution beyond v1's emphasis on acceleration with preserved quality and its untested distillation compatibility.

C2.justification: v2 adds covariate-shift and KL-divergence explanations for asymmetric reduction and similarity selection. Its limitations newly identify per-model hyperparameter tuning and weak acceleration for shorter image sequences. The earlier statement that distillation integration remains unexplored is superseded by the FastVideo evaluation.

D1.justification: Appendix B and Table 6 disclose reduction thresholds and rates, percentile-based similarity normalization, and model-specific stride, cache and sampling settings. v2 also supplies a code-access link. These substantially expand reproducibility information, although v1's PyTorch version and A100 memory specification are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 substantially shortens the UNet and factorized-DiT history and repositions token reduction around a claimed theoretical gap in prior methods. It adds the nearest-neighbor divergence reference, LPIPS and FastVideo, and emphasizes compatibility with few-step distillation. Mochi-1 and HunyuanVideo were already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The abstract, related work and method narrative are extensively rewritten. Method subsections are reorganized around matching theory, scheduling precedes caching, several discussions move into appendices, and the former discussion section becomes a focused limitations section with a separate impact statement.

P2.justification: v2 adds a prominent opening comparison figure, enlarges and rearranges the perturbation and method diagrams, changes the similarity plot from a two-by-two arrangement to one row, and replaces and expands qualitative panels. Main result tables are reorganized, older displays move into appendices, and new scheduling and VBench-dimension tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: Broader model validation, the previously untested six-step distillation integration, and explicit scheduling details improve empirical support and reproducibility. However, Appendix A's extension from i.i.d. sampling to covariance stationarity does not establish the dependence conditions needed for its consistency argument. The new blanket lower-LPIPS claim also conflicts with AsymRnR-fast's 0.5632 versus ToMe-fast's 0.5602 in Table 1. These weaknesses temper the overall gain.
